Subject: Request: streaming endpoint TTFT & sustained token/sec exception (LumenPoint POC)

Marcus —

Thanks for the demo last week. Our engineering team ran a short run against the streaming endpoint and surfaced two constraints that are important for our compliance and UX goals on the POC:

1) Time-to-first-token (TTFT): for our use case we need consistent sub-400ms TTFT for replies under 60 tokens (we see tail spikes today around ~700ms).
2) Sustained token/sec: during sustained extraction jobs we expect sustained output around 30-40 tokens/sec per connection. Your default streaming appears tuned for burst-first-token, but our workload is long-running chunked outputs.

We understand this may be outside standard hosted SLAs. Can Redwood provide an exception or a carve-out for the POC (4 weeks) with explicit TTFT and sustained token/sec commitments? We can accommodate a higher per-token price for the carve-out.

Attaching a short CSV with a sample of our traces.

Regards,

Oliver — thanks for the trace and the clear ask. We want the POC to succeed and we're open to a scoped exception, but I want to be explicit about a few constraints so procurement and engineering have the right expectations: 

- Redwood hosted streaming (default) is optimized for low TTFT across short responses. For medium/long-form outputs there's a tradeoff between TTFT and sustained per-connection throughput due to batching and scheduling.
- Typical hosted behavior: median TTFT in the 150–350ms range for concise responses; sustained token/s vary widely by model (10–80 t/s depending on model and quantization).

Proposed path for a 4-week POC exception: 
1) Canary profile: we'll provision a dedicated streaming class for your org (not a full Dedicated contract) and set a POC SLA: median TTFT <= 400ms at 95th pct <= 750ms for responses <60 tokens, and guaranteed sustained throughput of 30 tokens/sec per connection for sustained jobs with up to 8 concurrent connections.
2) Fallback and safety: if the streaming pool can't maintain the sustained rate, traffic will transparently failover to an equivalent sync endpoint (same model family) and we will record all failovers for the weeklies. The sync fallback will maintain total throughput but will not meet streaming TTFT.
3) Cost/disposition: the carve-out carries a POC uplift (one-time provisioning + margin) — I can give numbers once procurement confirms expected qps and concurrency.

Technical notes: to meet sustained rates we may recommend disabling some batching windows, enabling KV prefix caching for repeated prompts, and possibly a quantized variant of the model. I'll loop in Karthik for the fine tuning options (cc'd).

If the above sounds reasonable, Evelyn will draft an SLA addendum we can sign quickly.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Senior Product Manager, Redwood Inference

Oliver / Marcus —

Quick technical follow-up on options to hit the 30 t/s sustained target without compromising TTFT too much: 

- Model variant: switching to a smaller decoder variant or an INT8 quantized build can improve sustained throughput ~1.5–3x depending on prompt complexity.
- KV/prefix caching: if your workload repeats prompt headers or system tokens we can cache the KV for active sessions; that reduces per-request compute and improves TTFT for subsequent requests.
- Batching windows: we can reduce batching latency (smaller batch window) at the cost of lower GPU efficiency; we'll tune this for the 4-week POC.
- Concurrency shaping: reserve up to 8 dedicated streams for LumenPoint; for very high sustained throughput we recommend splitting across more shorter-lived streams rather than single long connection per job.

I've attached a CSV with microbenchmarks from our staging cluster (same as the one Marcus referenced). If you can share expected sustained qps and average output length we can produce a narrower config and an estimated cost uplift.

Thanks,
Karthik
Principal Engineer, Inference Runtime
